note.question: How should a medium allocate advertising and content over time when media technology constrains its control, consumers choose where to direct attention, and the medium cannot perfectly observe ad processing?
note.overview: The paper explicitly defines a continuous-time game between a medium and a consumer. The medium steers attention through format-constrained allocation actions, the consumer observes those actions and chooses attention, and equilibrium jointly solves their interdependent dynamic policies.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At each continuous time t, the medium chooses an allocation d(t) allowed by its format: simultaneous ad and content under static, either ad or content under sequential, or all three choices under interactive advertising. The consumer observes d(t) and chooses whether to attend to the ad, consume content, or take an outside option. A product-match signal may arrive while the ad is processed, after which attention and medium policy continue. The equilibrium solves the medium's allocation and the consumer's attention policy together. format-constrained continuous-time media allocation consumer attention response under stochastic information arrival
